body:
Synchronous generation currently occupies R's foreground thread. D-037 adds `llm_generate(async = TRUE, on_progress = ...)`, returning a standard promise while a native worker reuses the loaded model/context, plus `llm_cancel(m)` for cooperative cancellation. A process-wide execution permit prevents overlapping native access; R objects, RNG, progress callbacks and promise settlement stay on R's main thread. Work is bounded to one active job with no queue, and close/GC/shutdown preserve native ownership.

This is a development milestone, not a release. It adds only the approved optional later/promises dependencies and their scoped transitive exception; no Rust dependency or vendor patch. The ordinary synchronous result remains unchanged. Namespace shutdown frees native resources while keeping the DLL mapped for surviving finalizers; forced DLL unmapping is unsupported.

Validation:
- Local clippy, async debug/release, full default native goldens, FFI tests and final formatting passed.
- Six real cached-VLM cancellation/recovery/destruction boundary cases passed. These do not claim interruption inside synchronous C calls.
- All 35 R async/lifecycle/memory cases passed: 1,355 expectations, no skips or failures. Remaining package tests passed 1,177 expectations with 48 explicit model/environment skips.
- Fresh installation, source build and scoped package check passed with no errors. Two warnings reflect intentionally omitted rendered vignettes; final CI retains the full package/vignette matrix.
- The initial callback error and sandbox Metal failures are retained. The lazy callback condition was corrected and regression-tested; Metal was rerun with actual GPU access. No tolerance changed.

Initial CI at `1bd29c0` passed seven checks (all Rust/structural jobs and both Linux R legs), but both Mac R legs exceeded the lifecycle-child timeout. Oldrel also left a responsiveness fixture pending, followed by busy conditions. The diagnostic follow-up adds child stage timing and pending-worker counters, preserves failed scripts/logs, and changes no product code, timeout or assertion. The affected tests pass locally (1,313 expectations; four explicit model skips). Diagnostic `c8c7cff` localized the child timeout to the first synchronous CPU model load, before any async work: 37.561 s elapsed versus about 0.135 s CPU on oldrel. The follow-up separates a 90 s setup budget from the original 30 s lifecycle budget and 10 s drain limit, with explicit phase assertions and a 120 s outer watchdog. Other tests and all product code remain unchanged; local targeted checks pass and remote confirmation is pending. The underlying native/OS initialization wait and the earlier non-reproduced responsiveness outlier remain unexplained; original results are retained.

Keep this PR in draft until the actual foreground RStudio acceptance and all nine final CI checks pass. RStudio acceptance awaits the founder unlocking the Mac. The separate skill/planning PR #53 remains pending explicit merge consent; its historical D-037 proposal must not override the approved decision recorded here. WP10, I1 and release work are out of scope.

Implementation, acceptance boundaries and lossless local receipts: `docs/wp9-implementation.md`, `docs/wp9-async-plan.md`, and `tests/async/measurements/macos-arm64-2026-10-01/`.
